description: Shot boundary detection over the 480p proxy. Produces the shot ids MomentRecords sit inside; a moment never crosses a shot boundary, because crossing one is a cut and cuts belong to the planner.

normalisation.calibration_note: sigmoid output is already a probability per frame

notes:
Windows overlap by 25 frames on each side; only the centre 50 predictions of each 100-frame window are kept, because the model is unreliable at window edges. Raw pixel values in [0,255] with no normalisation -- this model does its own scaling internally, and applying a mean/std here silently degrades it.

NO ONNX AT THE DECLARED SOURCE (checked 2026-08-17 via the GitHub API). soCzech/TransNetV2 ships a TensorFlow SavedModel under inference/transnetv2-weights/ (git-LFS), a PyTorch conversion SCRIPT under inference-pytorch/ with no checkpoint beside it, and no GitHub releases at all. There is nothing named transnetv2.onnx to fetch, so scripts/models/fetch_weights.py reports this entry UNAVAILABLE and source_url stays a provenance link. Getting this file means running an export (tf2onnx over the SavedModel, or the PyTorch conversion then torch.onnx) and pinning OUR export -- at which point the artifact is ours and its digest is the only provenance it will ever have.

BATCHING (issue #31): DEMOTED TO 1, UNVERIFIED. This entry declared supported=true, max_batch=4, dynamic_axes=true. weights.blake3 is null, so the ONNX graph it names has never been produced or hashed, let alone had its input shape read -- the claim was an assumption wearing the clothes of a measurement, which is the same defect issue #31 found in the YuNet entry. Restore it by running onnxruntime.InferenceSession(...).get_inputs()[0].shape against the pinned checkpoint and recording that in batching.verified_against. Declining to batch costs throughput and nothing else.
